title: Why are the words sharp and blunt used for angles?
description: The words acute and obtuse mean sharp and blunt. An acute angle and an obtuse angle are drawn and shaded side by side, and the shape of the shaded corner shows why each word was chosen. The check opens the arms of the acute angle slowly to watch the point turn blunt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a small opening makes a thin sharp point, and a large opening makes a wide blunt corner. Watch for children who look at the length of the arms instead of the opening.

video_script.why: The child links the words acute and obtuse to the size of the opening, so the names are easy to remember.
video_script.substitution: An acute angle and an obtuse angle drawn with the space between their arms shaded.
video_script.anchor: an acute angle and an obtuse angle drawn side by side with the space between their arms shaded
video_script.payoff_line: An acute angle has a small opening, so its corner looks sharp. An obtuse angle has a large opening, so its corner looks blunt.

final_answer.value: acute angles have a smaller opening, so they look sharp; obtuse angles have a larger opening, so they look blunt
final_answer.spoken: an acute angle has a small opening, so its corner looks sharp, and an obtuse angle has a large opening, so its corner looks blunt

maths_rules: acute: opening smaller than a right angle, so the shaded wedge ends in a thin point, sharp
obtuse: opening bigger than a right angle, so the shaded wedge is wide at the corner, blunt
as the opening grows from small to large, the point goes from sharp to blunt
video_script.design: The two shaded angles stay side by side. The check opens the arms of the acute angle slowly so the child sees sharp turn into blunt.
